# `Browser.WakeLock`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.WakeLock — acquire a screen wake lock (preventing the device
from dimming or sleeping) and release it, over `Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: an outbound `JsCmd` acquires or releases the wake lock, and an
inbound `JsMsg` carries the outcome. Both cross the same seal codec and
fail-closed port discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses
`js-port:wake-lock` (import-derived, keyed on the canonical
`Ipe.Browser.WakeLock` path prefix via `WebCapability::for_browser_module`,
alias-immune); only the top-level app's `[capabilities] accepts` set can grant
it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.WakeLock.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound ADTs.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `acquire` returns a `Task Error ()`
    via the correlated port→Task bridge; `release` is fire-and-forget
    `Cmd`-shaped. The inbound `case` is EXHAUSTIVE: an unavailability or
    denial becomes a typed `Err`, never a silently dropped frame.

## `acquire`

```ipe
acquire : Task Error ()
```

`acquire` — request a screen wake lock, as a `Task Error ()`.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). Resolves with `Ok ()`
when the lock is held; resolves with a typed `Err` when the API is absent or
the browser denies the request (e.g. the page is not visible).

Importing this module discloses `js-port:wake-lock`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort WakeLock ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `release`

```ipe
release : Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`release` — release the currently held wake lock, fire-and-forget. A no-op
when no wake lock is held. Outbound `Cmd`.
